chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sacrificed thirty-six with his own hand, and Ali (peace be upon him) sacrificed what remained.' I said, 'Thirty-seven?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.نَحَرَ: Sacrificed (specifically camels by cutting the throat)

ai.seo_question: How many camels did the Prophet Muhammad sacrifice personally during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the ritual of *Nahr* (sacrificing camels) performed by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and Imam Ali (peace be upon him) during Hajj, emphasizing their direct participation in the act. While the Arabic text explicitly mentions sixty-three camels for the Prophet and thirty-seven for Ali, the summary reflects a specific scholarly interpretation or variant reading regarding the distribution of these sacrifices. This narration underscores the continuity of prophetic ritual practice through the Imams, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> sacrificed thirty-six (camels) with his<sup>saww</sup> own hands and Ali<sup>asws</sup> sacrificed what remained’. I said, ‘Thirty-seven?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthaman who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘The messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, slaughtered sixty-three heads of cattle with his own hand; and Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, slaughtered the rest.’ I then asked, ‘Was it thirty- seven ?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘Yes. It was thirty-seven.”
